product.olivetti-m20.summary: Olivetti’s professional Z8001 and PCOS desktop, preceding the M24’s move towards IBM compatibility.
product.olivetti-m20.history: Presented in March 1982, the M20 opened a new chapter in Olivetti’s professional range after the P6060 and P6040. It was a new project, developed with the OATC centre in Cupertino and manufactured in Italy; Docutel/Olivetti distributed it in the United States. Its PCOS environment set it apart from IBM compatibles. The M24 of 1984 subsequently took the 8086 and MS-DOS route. Sources: Olivetti Historical Archive, “Un computer su ogni scrivania”, and Sergio Mello-Grand, BYTE, June 1983, pp. 188–192.
product.olivetti-m20.warning: Historical sheet under research; no M20 platform or creation profile in BluMach.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.identity: Published dates do not necessarily refer to the same milestone. The Olivetti Historical Archive dates the presentation to March 1982 and BYTE confirms spring 1982; MAME records 1981 and 1000 BiT gives 1983. These references are retained without inferring alternative launches.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.memory: Memory expansion used proprietary boards. The manual specifies 128 KB on the motherboard and three 32 KB boards to reach 224 KB, or three 128 KB boards to reach 512 KB; this is not memory wholly available to programs.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.video: The display shares system memory. Resolution is 512 × 256; the manual allocates 16 KB for monochrome, 32 KB for four colours and 64 KB for eight. Colour configurations require the corresponding expansion boards and settings.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.apb: An optional board allowed software for another processor to run. The APB 1086 adds an 8086 for MS-DOS and CP/M-86; it does not turn the base M20 into an IBM PC. The manual requires checking the board revision and, for level D, replacing PA61/PA62 1.0 with PA77/PA78 2.0 and changing ZA–2 to ZA–1.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.firmware: The ROM starts and checks the machine before loading the system from disk. Olivetti documents 8 KB of EPROM; 1000 BiT writes “64Kb (16Kb × 4 ROM)”, which is not interpreted as 64 KB. The preserved PA61/PA62 files, 4 KiB each, match MAME BIOS 1.0 when interleaved. Versions 2.0d, 2.0f and APB remain references awaiting acquisition.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.verified: The documentation and ROM files have been checked without running the machine. The PA61/PA62 SHA-256 hashes match their receipt and the interleaved SHA-1 matches MAME 1.0. This does not establish bootability or physical donor provenance. BluMach offers no M20 machine or creation profile.
product.olivetti-m20.technical.limitatio: The sheet does not yet allow the machine to be created or booted. A Z8001 platform must be integrated and validated, including memory, video, keyboard, disks, ports and resets. ROMs 2.0d, 2.0f and APB are pending; PA61/PA62 have no antivirus scan or corroborated donor. External MAME support is not BluMach validation.
